title.value: A Survey on Model MoErging: Recycling and Routing Among Specialized Experts for Collaborative Learning
title.justification: The title explicitly states the survey's focus on Model MoErging, highlighting the concepts of recycling, routing, and collaborative learning.
title.quote: A Survey on Model MoErging: Recycling and Routing Among Specialized Experts for Collaborative Learning

analysis.description: This paper provides a comprehensive survey on Model MoErging, which involves recycling fine-tuned expert models to create aggregate systems with improved performance or generalization. It introduces a taxonomy to categorize main design choices for MoErging methods, discusses related research fields, and inventories relevant software tools.

type.justification: The paper examines various MoErging methods, presents a taxonomy, and reviews existing research and applications, indicating empirical work.
type.quote: Our survey provides a unified overview of existing MoErging methods and creates a solid foundation for future work in this burgeoning field.

name.justification: The paper focuses on Model MoErging, a collaborative learning approach using specialized expert models, making it a part of collaborative learning systems.
name.quote: Model MoErging involves recycling fine-tuned expert models to create aggregate systems.

name.justification: The paper frequently discusses the relationship between MoErging and mixture-of-experts (MoE) models.
name.quote: These methods have been referred to as “MoErging” since they frequently share methodology and ideas with mixture-of-experts (MoE) models.

name.justification: The paper discusses overlaps with multitask learning, specifically using models for various tasks.
name.quote: Multitask Learning aims to solve multiple tasks simultaneously, usually with a single model.

name.justification: The paper describes MoErging as related to model merging techniques, which involves combining independently trained models.
name.quote: Model merging aims to combine independently trained models that share an architecture into a single model.

name.justification: The paper describes AdapterFusion as a method involving task-specific adapters and attention modules to improve in-distribution performance.
name.quote: AdapterFusion: Non-destructive task composition for transfer learning.

is_contributed.justification: AdapterFusion is referenced in the context of existing methods related to MoErging, but not as a new contribution within this survey.
is_contributed.quote: Pfeiffer et al. (2021) propose a two-stage algorithm.

is_executed.justification: The execution of models (on GPU/CPU) is not mentioned in the survey's description of AdapterFusion.
is_executed.quote: Their experiment on 16 natural language understanding tasks shows in-distribution performance improvement on 12 tasks.

is_compared.justification: AdapterFusion's performance is compared to standard full model fine-tuning, showing better results in in-distribution tasks.
is_compared.quote: Their experiment on 16 natural language understanding tasks shows in-distribution performance improvement.
